Subject: Re: Observed streaming errors + latency spikes (Brightline Prod)

Hi Aditya / Lauren,

We're seeing a steady uptick in streaming errors from our production workload starting ~2028-03-14 22:00 PST. Symptoms: ~10-15% of streaming sessions terminate with grpc-like errors (client sees stream end + error code), p99 token latency jumps to 9-12s (normally ~120ms), and throughput backpressure that causes our ingestion pipelines to stall. We captured a short sample of request IDs and timestamps in the attached CSV.

Impact: billing window for our March deployment is this week — this is blocking traffic for ~30% of service endpoints. Our infra team suspects middleboxes/proxies could be adding or rewriting HTTP/2 trailers but haven't confirmed. Can Redwood run an urgent triage?

Sample request IDs (from CSV): BRG-req-20280314-01, BRG-req-20280314-09, BRG-req-20280314-44

We've attached a small tcpdump excerpt that shows multiple FIN/stream errors. Happy to jump on a call — earliest availability between 10:30–12:00 PDT today.

Thanks,
Kristen Dawson
Head of Integrations
Brightline Health

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwoodinference.com>
To: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwoodinference.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwoodinference.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Thu, 15 Mar 2028 12:18:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: [INTERNAL] Brightline streaming P1 — initial analysis

Quick update from runtime: we've reproduced a similar symptom in our lab using a proxy that appends HTTP/2 trailer frames (common when gateways append small status trailers). Root cause (short): client SDK v1.8.2's streaming parser assumes trailers are delivered as a single, coalesced HEADERS frame and does not tolerate fragmented/trailing HEADERS frames interleaved with DATA frames. When an intermediary reorders or fragments trailer frames, our parser treats the first fragment as malformed leading to a stream abort and partial KV-cache loss that triggers long tail latency on retry.

Two paths forward (short-term & medium-term):
1) Short-term mitigation (can be shipped as a runtime/SDK toggle today): expose a client-side flag (--tolerate-fragmented-trailers=true) that enables a more permissive header reassembly code path. We have a Canary build with that flag in a branch: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/1984. This avoids aborts but slightly increases memory for some edge cases.
2) Medium-term fix: harden the streaming parser in SDK v1.9.0 (breaking change for a couple of legacy adapters) and release a server-side fallback that accepts fragmented HEADERS/trailer sequences gracefully. Target: canary rollout in 24–48 hours, full rollout 7 days after successful validation.

I'll prepare a backout plan and a diagnostic script to validate a request path for trailer fragmentation. Jonas — can you enable deeper ingress tracing for BRG traffic and capture a 30-minute window?

— Rishi
Senior Software Engineer, Runtime

Date: Fri, 16 Mar 2028 09:22:00 -07:00
Subject: Mitigation & timeline for Brightline — streaming failures

Hi Kristen — quick update following our triage.

What we found: Rishi's team reproduced the failure and traced it to trailer/frame fragmentation introduced by certain HTTP/2-terminating proxies. Our current SDK (v1.8.2) is strict about trailer coalescing and can abort streams when fragments arrive out of the expected pattern.

Immediate mitigation (what we will do for Brightline this week):
- Tomorrow 08:00–10:00 PDT we will push a canary runtime and SDK toggle (--tolerate-fragmented-trailers=true) to the Brightline tenant. This is non-breaking and reversible; it re-enables a permissive header reassembly path.
- We will ask Brightline to route a small percentage (5–10%) of traffic through the canary for 2 hours and confirm errors drop and p99 returns to baseline.
- If positive, we will widen the canary to 25% then 100% over 24 hours.

Longer term: SDK v1.9.0 (parser hardening) will be released in ~7 days and the runtime will include defensive parsing on the service-side.

Attachments: mitigation-guide.pdf (steps to validate, how to opt in/out of canary)

Can you confirm the 08:00–10:00 PDT window tomorrow for the 5–10% canary? If that works we'll schedule a short status call at +30m into the window.

Thanks for patience — we'll own the remediation until Brightline is back to normal.

— Aditya
